name: Thornwood
description: Floriated woodcut letters with sharp medieval silhouettes and original lobed thorn leaves, cut veins, rosettes, branch spirals and double keylines.
design_changes: Extracted only the interior historic letter body from each Morris initial; removed every original outer foliage and frame component.
Renormalized body proportions and redrew the ornamental composition from new path data.
Added original cut-vein lobed thorn foliage, per-letter seeded leaf positions, branch spirals, two rosettes and outer letter keylines.
Added sparse new engraved cuts to the thick letter strokes; preserved E’s separately encoded crossbar.

name: Scriptorium
description: Illuminated penwork versals with historic blackletter anatomy, newly incised stem scrolls and extensive open curling pen sprays.
design_changes: Reconstructed the Royal historic silhouettes with a closing operation and selective counter preservation, removing and merging fine source ornament.
Added new engraved S-scroll cuts throughout available stem interiors.
Recomposed open spaces with eight original calligraphic branching sprays, lobed leaf terminals and ink beads.
Replaced the original visual composition with a wider freely branching penwork silhouette.

name: Ribbon
description: Insular letters rebuilt as channeled bands and threaded with original alternating over-and-under interlace strands.
design_changes: Isolated Carrick’s weighty insular letter construction with a morphological opening; removed most original thin interlace and outline details.
Discarded tiny remnant components and rebuilt body edges with a light closing operation.
Cut new inset channels following the complete letter contours and counters.
Drew three new continuous ornamental strands and two foreground crossing segments; erased the understrands at the crossings to make genuine interlace.

Preserved historical letter identity and roof/foot construction while materially replacing the ornament; independently redrew I and T for distinct anatomy, strengthened E’s exposed middle arm, and extended Q’s tail.

name: Iris
description: Hand-drawn plant-stem capitals, iris flowers, elongated leaves, and whiplash tendrils.
design_changes: 26 original hand-drawn curved letter skeletons expanded into contrasting tapered ribbons.
Per-letter rooted leaf terminals, iris-petal drawings, and whiplash vine arrangement.
Actual transparent engraving and clear letter/ornament interlace.

name: Laurel
description: Bowed high-contrast Roman outlines with engraved hatching, rooted laurel sprays, blossom clusters, and berries.
design_changes: Illustration-specific bowed contour geometry and asymmetric organic contour fitting in every capital.
Entirely new rooted laurel leaf/flower/berry compositions per letter, including counter ornament.
Engraved letter interior hatch, outlined face, and transparent separation from plants.

name: Briar
description: Broad light capitals cut transparently through a dense Arts-and-Crafts canopy of dog roses, leaves, and intertwined thorn stems.
design_changes: Illustration-specific broad fitting, bowed stems, and curved waist treatment in every capital.
Entirely new dense dog-rose canopy, original lobed flower geometry and lanceolate leaves.
Capital is negative-space cut through artwork, with open transparent leaf veins and no white paint.

name: Nocturne
description: Blackletter capitals with pressure-written flourishes, quill-cut highlights, and fitted counter arabesques.
design_changes: Individually fitted cap proportions; broad capitals retain a full optical cap height.
New quill-cut interior contours preserve the blackletter silhouettes and counters.
Original pressure-shaped pennants, linked scrolls, spirals and leaf-like pen terminals attach to the individual letter outlines.
Counter arabesques are fitted only where clear interior room exists.
Different terminal groups fit curved, diagonal and upright capitals; Q has a substantial new diagonal descending swash and J has an enlarged hooked terminal.

name: Cameo
description: Relief-engraved Roman capitals with inset glints, diagonal graver shading, and fitted laurel or acanthus terminals.
design_changes: Reconstructed capital proportions retain the full cap height for M and W.
A new offset extruded side plane is separated from the letter face by transparent air.
Inset left-edge glints and diagonal graver channels are Boolean cuts, with no opaque white paint.
Original engraved laurel sprays, split-leaf acanthus volutes, intertwined ribbons and small intaglio seals fit four structural letter groups.

name: Obelisk
description: Original Art Deco capitals with chamfered bowls, low crossbars, fluted stems, and stepped terminal collars.
design_changes: All 26 semantic skeletons are independently authored as coordinates.
Low A and H bars, a high-waisted K, chamfered B/D/O/P/R bowls, and a diagonal Q tail define the architecture.
Parallel transparent cuts run through the letter strokes themselves to create three fluted rails.
Stepped collars attach only to actual open terminals; narrow sunburst and needle ornaments do not form a box.

name: Tessera
description: Original faceted capitals with broad black strokes, forked spear terminals, and transparent geometric inlays. Nested lozenges, chevrons, and angular fragments suggest cut tesserae arranged along each stroke.
design_changes: Drew a complete original A–Z structure as polygonal stroke centerlines with letter-specific proportions.
Used asymmetrical, faceted bowl construction and flat-topped pointed forms.
Added integral split spear terminals to the silhouette, rather than a frame around unchanged lettering.
Subtracted lozenge, chevron, triangular, and diagonal-joint motifs from the ink geometry; preserved nested black inset stones.
Cut real transparent inlays and counters with Boolean geometry and even-odd SVG paths.
Added 44-unit safety margins around the full ink bounds for every letter, including Q's descending terminal.
